lesson_title: The Kakatiya Empire: Rise and Fall

scenes.teacher_script: Hello students! Today, we will explore the fascinating history of the Kakatiya Empire, a significant regional kingdom that emerged in South India.
The Kakatiya kingdom arose in Warangal between 1000 and 1350 CE. This period was crucial for the development of regional kingdoms and the first Telugu books.
The Kakatiya kings were great builders, as seen in the magnificent Kirti Torana, the entrance to the Svayambhu Siva Temple in Warangal.

template_data.image_prompt: High-quality realistic photograph of the Kirti Torana entrance of Svayambhu Siva Temple in Warangal, India, showcasing intricate carvings and historical architecture. Sunny day, clear sky, 16:9 ratio, educational diagram style.

scenes.teacher_script: They also issued their own currency, like the 'Sri Ahita gaja kesari' gold coin, which provides valuable insights into their rule and symbols.

template_data.image_prompt: High-quality realistic photograph of a historical gold coin issued by the Kakatiya dynasty, specifically the 'Sri Ahita gaja kesari' coin, showing detailed ancient script and an elephant emblem. Macro shot, clean white background, 16:9 ratio, educational diagram style.

scenes.teacher_script: The Kakatiya dynasty eventually came to an end in 1323 CE. Sultan Mohammad bin Tugluq defeated Kakatiya Prataparudra, marking the end of their rule.
